steps.do: List the existing test files in the project.
List the available iOS simulator devices to choose a destination.
Plan a measure block that types 10 characters into the TextField and records the time for each keystroke.
Set the budget at 16ms per keystroke for 60Hz devices, and 8ms for ProMotion 120Hz devices.
Run the input performance test class on the chosen simulator.

K-017002.example: A TextField typing test records 10 keystrokes that average 4.2ms each, which passes the 16ms budget for 60Hz devices. The test fails the build if the average goes above 16ms.
K-017002.check: xcodebuild prints Test Suite 'InputPerfTests' passed, and the measured average per keystroke is below 16ms.
traps: Measures app launch time with XCTest measure instead of keystroke time, so the result does not test the input.
Uses the 16ms budget for ProMotion displays, where the frame budget is 8ms.

steps.do: Print the number of terminal columns available to the table; expect a number such as 120 when run inside tmux, not 80 with no terminal attached.
Write the plan rule that the table width equals the terminal columns minus the border cells.
Compute the per-column maximum for 120 columns, 6 border cells, and 5 columns, rounded down; the expected output is 22.
Count the flat string keys in the English file so the plan knows how many labels must fit.

K-017003.example: If tput cols prints 120 and the table has 5 columns with 6 border cells, each column gets (120 - 6) / 5, which rounds down to 22 cells. The plan then truncates any translated label longer than 22 cells.
K-017003.check: Step 1 prints the terminal width, such as 120, step 3 prints 22, and step 4 prints a count equal to the number of flat keys in en.json.
traps: tput cols prints 80 when no terminal is attached, so run the check inside tmux.
Forgetting the border cells makes the table overflow the right edge.
Truncate by cells, not characters, or wide labels still overflow.

steps.do: List every input control in the Sources folder.
List the state properties those controls bind to.
Count input controls per file to set the baseline.
Measure the line count of each Swift file; any parent body file of 200 lines or more is a split candidate.
Create the plan file that lists one child view per input found above.

K-017004.example: The search screen has a TextField bound to @State searchText inside a 400-line body, so the plan moves it into a SearchField child view. Only SearchField then reads the changing value on each keystroke.
K-017004.check: rg prints each input site as file:line, the plan lists one child view for each parent @State bound to an input, for example 3 children for 3 inputs, and wc -l reports any parent file of 200 lines or more as a split candidate.
traps: Assumes every @State change redraws the whole screen; SwiftUI only invalidates views that read the changed value.
Moves the state into a child but still passes the whole model down, so the parent still reads it.

steps.do: Find every onChange handler in the sources.
Find every place that starts a Task from an input.
Find every existing .task(id:) modifier on the search field.
Find every Task.sleep call so the debounce delay is visible in one list.
Confirm the 300 millisecond value appears only once in the sources.
Run the test suite for your scheme on the iPhone simulator; the plan adds a test that expects 1 request for 5 keystrokes 300ms apart.

K-017005.example: Typing 'swift' in one second changes searchText 5 times, so the debounce sends 1 request 300ms after the last key instead of 5. The 300ms constant is written in one place so it can be tuned later.

K-017006.check: grep -rc prints a count of 5 or fewer @State declarations for each parent file in the plan, wc -l flags any Form file of 200 lines or more, and the xcodebuild build reports 0 errors.

steps.do: List every file that renders a native select element.
Count select-related disabled classes already used in the project.

Confirm whether the project has tailwind.config.js or only a CSS entry file.

K-017010.example: rg -l prints src/components/CountrySelect.tsx and src/forms/RegionSelect.tsx, and npm ls prints tailwindcss@3.4.x, so size-4 is available. The plan then reuses the existing disabled:opacity-60 pattern.
K-017010.check: rg -l prints one path per select file, and npm ls prints a tailwindcss line with a version number; if it prints empty, add tailwindcss to the plan before build.
traps: Small models assume Tailwind v4 syntax without checking, then write @theme or @apply code that a v3 project does not read.
Skipping the inventory creates a second select style with different disabled colors in the same app.

steps.do: Write five states, idle, loading, empty, error, and loaded, each with one row describing the select behavior.
Map the loading state to disabled plus disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60 and aria-busy:cursor-progress.
Confirm the installed Tailwind version supports the disabled and aria-busy variants.
Create the plan file that will hold the state matrix.

K-017011.example: The loading row is disabled with aria-busy='true' and classes disabled:opacity-60 aria-busy:cursor-progress. The empty row keeps the select enabled and shows a single option labeled No options.
K-017011.check: npm ls prints a tailwindcss version of 3.2 or newer, and ls docs/select-loading-plan.md prints the file path after touch runs.
traps: Small models forget the error row, so a failed fetch leaves the select stuck in the loading style.
The disabled attribute blocks focus, so the plan must also define a visible status message instead of relying on the select alone.

steps.do: Wrap the select in a container with the classes relative group.
List existing components folder contents to find where the spinner icon should live.
Place the spinner as a sibling with absolute right-8 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 pointer-events-none classes.
Size the spinner with size-4, which is 1rem or 16px at the default root font size, and set text-gray-500 for color.
Confirm the select height target uses h-11, which is 44px, by searching for existing uses.

K-017012.example: The wrapper is div class='relative group', and the spinner is svg class='absolute right-8 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 size-4 text-gray-500 pointer-events-none animate-spin'. The select keeps h-11 so its tap target stays 44px.
K-017012.check: ls src/components lists the folder, and rg -n 'h-11' src returns zero matches at plan stage or the existing lines that use it; after build the select must have h-11 for 44px.

Forgetting pointer-events-none lets the spinner block clicks on the dropdown arrow.

steps.do: Set the spinner wrapper to opacity-0 with transition-opacity duration-150 delay-200 so it fades in after 200ms.
Show the spinner with group-data-[loading=true]:opacity-100 on the group wrapper when the loading flag is set.
Count existing delay-200 uses in the project to match its convention.
Check existing transition classes in the project to confirm duration-150 is the house value.

K-017013.example: The spinner wrapper uses opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-150 delay-200 and group-data-[loading=true]:opacity-100. A fetch that takes 120ms never shows the spinner.
K-017013.check: rg -c 'delay-200' src prints a count per file that uses it, or nothing at plan stage, and the plan lists a 200ms delay in the spinner row.
traps: Small models forget that delay-200 also delays the fade-out, so the spinner lingers 200ms after loading ends.
group-data-[loading=true] needs the data-loading attribute on the parent group element, not on the spinner itself.

steps.do: Add a visually hidden status element with the classes sr-only and aria-live='polite' that announces Loading options.
Link the select to the status element with aria-describedby and set aria-busy='true' while loading.
List the Playwright tests that will exist once the project's test files are present, including loading disables select and error shows retry.
Confirm the tests directory exists before writing new test files into it.

K-017014.example: The status element is span id='select-status' class='sr-only' aria-live='polite', and the select sets aria-describedby='select-status' aria-busy='true'. The test list includes loading disables select, empty shows No options, and error shows Retry.
K-017014.check: npx playwright test --list prints the test names it finds, and ls tests prints the folder contents; at plan stage the list may be empty, so the plan must still name at least three tests.

Setting disabled alone removes the select from focus order, so the status text must carry the loading message.

steps.do: Find any Tailwind config file in the project up to two levels deep.
Check whether the config overrides the default screens.
List source files that already mention a modal or dialog.
If no screens override exists, use the default breakpoints sm 640px, md 768px, and lg 1024px.

K-017015.example: find prints ./tailwind.config.js and grep prints nothing, so the defaults apply. The plan is a full-width sheet below sm: and a centered dialog from sm: upward.
K-017015.check: grep -c 'screens' tailwind.config.js prints 0 when the defaults apply, and rg -l prints the paths of existing modal files.
traps: Assuming a tailwind.config.js exists in Tailwind v4, where breakpoints are set in an @theme block in CSS.
Writing max-sm: or max-md: when the plan needs mobile-first min-width prefixes like sm: and md:.
Choosing 1024px as the switch point without checking the project's own screens override.

steps.do: List the max-w classes already used in the source.
Count existing sm:max-w overrides so the plan matches the project's style.
Plan w-full with p-4 on mobile, sm:max-w-md at 640px, md:max-w-lg at 768px, and lg:max-w-2xl at 1024px.
Confirm the installed Tailwind defines these max-width values in its default config.

K-017016.example: The plan uses sm:max-w-md, which is 28rem or 448px, so on a 640px screen the dialog is 448px wide with 16px gutters on each side. The mobile base class is w-full with p-4 around the wrapper.
K-017016.check: rg -n 'maxWidth' prints the defaults, and max-w-md shows 28rem in the output.
traps: Skipping the p-4 gutter, which lets the modal touch the screen edges at 375px.
Using an arbitrary value like max-w-[448px] when the scale class max-w-md already exists.
Using max-w-screen-sm, which is a different idiom from the max-w-md scale value.

steps.do: Check whether the viewport meta tag already sets viewport-fit=cover.
List arbitrary bottom padding classes already in use.
Plan the sheet footer as pb-4 plus pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)] so the buttons clear the home indicator.
Plan the wrapper as fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 on mobile, with sm:inset-0 sm:m-auto for the centered dialog from 640px.

K-017017.example: The footer uses pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)], which resolves to 34px on an iPhone with a home indicator and 0px on devices without one. The sm: classes switch the wrapper back to a centered dialog at 640px.

Applying the safe-area padding to desktop centered dialogs, where it adds an unneeded gap.

steps.do: Check whether Playwright is installed in the project.
List existing Playwright spec files, skipping node_modules.
Plan four viewports: 375x667 for a phone, 640x800 for the sm edge, 768x1024 for md, and 1280x800 for desktop.
Plan one assertion per viewport that the dialog width is no more than the viewport width minus 32px.
Confirm the Playwright config already lists projects or viewport settings to hold these sizes.

Skipping the 640px edge, so the sm: switch is never tested.
Testing only the desktop viewport and missing the phone layout.

steps.do: Find modal panels that use h-screen or an arbitrary h-[...] height in the source.
Check for 100vh, which mobile browsers miscalculate when the toolbar shows or hides.
Plan the panel as max-h-[85dvh] overflow-y-auto so the content scrolls inside the panel.
Plan the wrapper as flex items-end sm:items-center so the panel docks to the bottom on phones and centers from 640px.

K-017019.check: rg -c 'max-h-\[85dvh\]' src prints 1 or more after the build, and 85% of 375px is 318.75px.

Using dvh without checking that the installed Tailwind version accepts the dvh arbitrary value.

steps.do: Open SignupForm.test.tsx and confirm it imports vi from vitest.
Add a test that mocks global fetch with vi.fn resolving to a Response with status 500.
Add afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks()) so the 500 mock does not leak into later tests.
In the test, fill valid email and password, await user.click on Submit, then assert screen.getByRole('alert') has text 'Something went wrong. Try again.'
Assert the Submit button is disabled while pending using await waitFor(() => expect(button).toBeDisabled()).
Run the test file and read the pass count. Expect 'Tests 2 passed' with no 'Unable to find role' errors.

K-017020.example: The mocked fetch returns status 500, so the component renders a div with role='alert' containing the server message. The test then expects the button to be disabled during pending and enabled after the error.
K-017020.check: Output shows 'Tests 2 passed' for the server error cases with no 'Unable to find role' errors.
traps: Small models often forget to restore the mock, so later tests inherit the 500 response; call vi.restoreAllMocks in afterEach.
Using getByText instead of getByRole('alert') does not prove the error is announced.
Forgetting to await the click lets the assertion run before the state update.

steps.do: Create the spec file tests/signup.spec.ts.
Write a test that imports test and expect from @playwright/test, opens /signup, clicks Submit, and expects a role='alert' element with text 'Email is required'.
Add a test that calls page.route('**/api/signup', route => route.fulfill({ status: 500 })) before submitting valid data and expects the server error alert.
Confirm playwright.config.ts sets webServer so the dev server starts before the tests run.
Run the Playwright spec with the line reporter. Read the summary: expect '2 passed' and no 'failed' line, with exit code 0.

K-017021.example: The first test clicks Submit on an empty form and finds the alert text 'Email is required'. The second test intercepts the POST with a 500 response and finds 'Something went wrong. Try again.' in the alert.
K-017021.check: Output ends with '2 passed' and no '1 failed' line, and the exit code is 0.
traps: Small models often start the test before the dev server runs, so the page times out; set webServer in playwright.config.ts or start npm run dev first.
Using page.waitForTimeout(1000) instead of expect(locator).toBeVisible() makes tests slow and flaky.
Hitting the real backend in the failure test makes the result depend on server state; always use page.route.

steps.do: Create the spec file tests/signup-target.spec.ts.
Write a test that imports test and expect from @playwright/test, opens /signup, and clicks Submit with empty fields.
In the test, read the bounding box of the Submit button using await button.boundingBox().
Assert that boundingBox.height and boundingBox.width are each at least 44.
Compute the contrast ratio of the error text color against its background and assert it is at least 4.5:1, since this is body-size text.
Run the spec with the line reporter. Read the summary: expect '1 passed' and both the size and contrast expects to succeed.

K-017022.example: The Submit button measures 48px by 44px, and the error text #b00020 on #ffffff gives a ratio of about 7.0:1. Both assertions pass in the Playwright run.
K-017022.check: Output shows '1 passed' and the test's expects for height >= 44 and contrast >= 4.5 both succeed.
traps: Small models often measure the contrast of the input border instead of the error text, which tests the wrong element.
Checking only the CSS height misses padding added by the button; use boundingBox, which reports rendered size.
Using a 4.5:1 threshold for large text is wrong for normal-size error text, so keep 4.5:1 for body-size text.

Add motion-reduce:animate-none so the spinner stops rotating when the user prefers reduced motion.
Show the text Loading options beside the icon, so the static state still communicates progress.
Count existing motion-reduce uses in the project to match the team convention.
Find existing animate-spin uses to confirm the spinner pattern.
Run the Playwright spinner test with reduced motion emulated; it must pass, showing the icon not rotating and the Loading options text visible.

Check whether any button already uses h-11 w-11 or h-10 w-10.

Check that the project sets aria-label on icon-only buttons.

K-017024.check: npx playwright test tests/close-button.spec.ts reports a boundingBox of 44px by 44px or more, and rg -c 'h-11 w-11' src prints 1 or more. 2.75rem equals 44px at the default 16px root size.

steps.do: Find where the focus duration constant is defined in the source tree.
Read the token file to see the duration value.
Run the token unit test that asserts focusDuration equals 0.2.
Confirm the run ended with a success line and exit code 0.

K-017025.example: MotionTokens.focusDuration is 0.2 and MotionTokens.focus is Animation.easeOut(duration: focusDuration). MotionTokenTests asserts XCTAssertEqual(MotionTokens.focusDuration, 0.2, accuracy: 0.001), so changing the value to 0.35 makes the test fail.

Running the whole suite without -only-testing, which hides the one result you need.
Reporting success without reading the token file first; the test may not cover the value you edited.

List withAnimation calls in the search field sources so unguarded ones are visible.
Run the Reduce Motion unit tests on the iPhone 16 simulator.
Confirm the output reports zero failures for the two tests.

Run the floating label snapshot tests on the iPhone 16 simulator.

Find where keyboard safe area handling is set in the search field sources.

Run the clear button UI test that waits for the button to disappear.
Confirm the test passed and that waitForNonExistence returned true within the 0.2 second timeout.

steps.do: Search for existing timers so two dismiss timers do not fight each other.
Set the default duration to 6000ms and the error duration to 0 so error toasts stay until the user dismisses them.
Plan to pause the timer on mouseenter and focusin and resume on mouseleave and focusout, per WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable.
Confirm the constant name for the default duration in the source tree.

K-017031.example: An info toast gets 6000ms, a focused toast holds its timer, and an error toast with duration 0 never auto-dismisses. The pause logic sits in onMouseEnter and onFocusIn in ToastItem.vue.
K-017031.check: rg DEFAULT_DURATION src prints one definition with the value 6000, and the plan lists the pause events in ToastItem.vue.
traps: Forgetting to clear the timer on unmount leaves a callback that removes a toast twice.
Setting a short timeout such as 2000ms fails users who read slowly or use assistive technology.

steps.do: Check whether any existing component calls focus on insert.
Plan that status toasts never move focus, because moving focus for a status message disrupts the user.
Plan a Teleport to body in ToastContainer.vue so the toast sits outside the page flow.
Give each dismiss button an aria-label that names the toast, for example Dismiss saved, and a minimum target size of 44px.
Run axe on the dev server once the component exists to confirm there are no button label or target size violations.

K-017032.example: Saving a file shows a status toast with a Dismiss saved button 44px tall, and focus stays on the Save button. Only a blocking modal error may move focus to its dialog.
